summary.title: DevSecOps Juice Shop Threat Model
summary.description: STRIDE threat model for the OWASP Juice Shop DevSecOps pipeline, including CI/CD security controls and hardened Kubernetes/Kind runtime controls.

threats.title: T01 - Compromised developer account
threats.description: An attacker compromises a developer identity and pushes unauthorized source code, workflow changes, or configuration.
threats.mitigation: Protect developer accounts with strong authentication, repository access controls, branch protection, and code review.

threats.title: T02 - Malicious source or configuration changes
threats.description: An attacker or compromised contributor modifies application code, Docker configuration, CI/CD workflows, or Kubernetes manifests.
threats.mitigation: Require pull requests, code review, protected branches, and security scanning before deployment.

threats.title: T03 - Malicious workflow modification
threats.description: A modified workflow bypasses security checks or executes attacker-controlled commands in the CI/CD runner.
threats.mitigation: Protect workflow files, require review, use least-privilege permissions, and monitor workflow changes.

threats.title: T04 - Dependency tampering
threats.description: A compromised or malicious dependency is introduced during the build process.
threats.mitigation: Use dependency scanning, lockfiles, controlled dependency updates, and review dependency changes.

threats.title: T05 - Secrets exposed in CI/CD
threats.description: Secrets present in source code or build output may be exposed to logs, artifacts, or CI/CD processes.
threats.mitigation: Use Gitleaks, avoid hard-coded secrets, protect CI/CD secrets, and prevent sensitive values from being logged.

threats.title: T08 - Vulnerable dependencies
threats.description: Known vulnerable packages may be included in the application dependency tree and become part of the deployed application.
threats.mitigation: Run Trivy filesystem/dependency scanning in CI and gate applicable high-risk findings.

threats.title: T09 - Exposed secrets
threats.description: Hard-coded credentials, tokens, or keys may be committed to the repository.
threats.mitigation: Run Gitleaks during CI and prevent real credentials from being committed.

threats.title: T06 - Insecure build configuration
threats.description: A malicious or insecure Dockerfile/build process could introduce vulnerable configuration or malicious content into the image.
threats.mitigation: Use a multistage Docker build, non-root runtime execution, minimal runtime image, and image scanning.

threats.title: T10 - Misconfigured Kubernetes manifests
threats.description: Insecure Kubernetes configuration could weaken runtime isolation or expose the application.
threats.mitigation: Run Checkov against Kubernetes manifests and review or remediate reported configuration issues.

threats.title: T11 - Malicious or vulnerable container image
threats.description: A vulnerable or tampered image could execute malicious code when deployed to Kubernetes.
threats.mitigation: Scan the image with Trivy and use a hardened non-root multistage runtime image.

threats.title: T12 - Container privilege escalation
threats.description: An attacker who compromises the application attempts to gain elevated privileges inside the container.
threats.mitigation: Run as non-root UID 65532, disable privilege escalation, and drop all Linux capabilities.

threats.title: T13 - Container escape
threats.description: A compromised container attempts to escape its isolation and affect the host or other workloads.
threats.mitigation: Use non-root execution, dropped capabilities, RuntimeDefault seccomp, and a read-only root filesystem.

threats.title: T14 - Kubernetes API access
threats.description: A compromised workload attempts to abuse Kubernetes ServiceAccount credentials to access the Kubernetes API.
threats.mitigation: Disable automatic ServiceAccount token mounting with automountServiceAccountToken: false.

threats.title: T16 - Resource exhaustion
threats.description: A compromised or abusive workload consumes excessive CPU or memory and impacts application availability.
threats.mitigation: Define CPU and memory requests and limits for the Juice Shop container.

threats.title: T15 - Unauthorized network access
threats.description: An unauthorized workload attempts to connect to the Juice Shop pod.
threats.mitigation: Use a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy that restricts ingress to the Juice Shop workload from the juice-shop namespace on TCP port 3000.
